annotation.title_clean: Directive 2000/70/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Council Directive 93/42/EEC as regards medical devices incorporating stable derivates of human blood or human plasma
annotation.title_en: Directive 2000/70/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Council Directive 93/42/EEC as regards medical devices incorporating stable derivates of human blood or human plasma
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Communities, L 313
annotation.summary_en: EU Directive of 16 November 2000 amending the Medical Devices Directive 93/42/EEC to bring devices incorporating human blood or plasma derivatives within its scope. It requires EMEA scientific opinion, batch testing and release certificates, labelling, and Class III classification. It has no AI or robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Devices incorporating a human blood derivative as an integral part fall under Directive 93/42/EEC.
Notified bodies must seek an EMEA scientific opinion on the derivative's quality and safety.
Manufacturers must send batch release certificates from a State laboratory to the notified body.
Such devices are classified as Class III and labelled as containing a human blood derivative.
Member States must transpose by 13 December 2001 and apply from 13 June 2002.
